businessReadSeam.targetAccess: Check target-specific permission before querying row by exact id; return original type-specific NotFound when absent. Original requireTargetAccess does not filter by owner or org. Do not invent a stronger row-scope rule during compatibility migration.
businessReadSeam.readAttachment: Attachment must be active, pass security gate and have at least one active link with target permission and a real existing row. canAccessAnyLink catches each target error and tries the next link; no uploader bypass here.
businessReadSeam.mutateAttachment: Original assertCanMutateAttachment accepts uploadedBy==user.sub; otherwise any active link with the type-level write permission suffices, without checking target existence here. Keep this distinct from read/access/link/unlink checks.
businessReadSeam.uploadOwner: If session.createdBy is non-null and different, deny before target reads. Non-null targetType+targetId use normal target access. Only when those are absent does baseAttachmentId fallback apply. Do not replace these ordered branches with one blanket ownership check.
businessReadSeam.security: Only confidential/restricted levels require any of contract:finance:sensitive:read, operating:finance:sensitive:read, commission:amount:sensitive:read, platform:roles:manage. Normal/internal/sensitive follow original behavior.
businessReadSeam.center: Only customer/lead/project/contract; latest active attachments linked to permitted target types, security filter, actual target lookup, suppress dangling targets, one row per targetType/targetId/attachmentId. targetOwnerName is currently null. Preserve linkage ordering and full attachment active-link summaries.
businessReadSeam.uploader: Read platform_user by actual uploadedBy IDs; displayName fallback username. Initial complete summaries explicitly have uploadedByName null while subsequent GET/list resolves the user.
businessReadSeam.R2EDependencies: Reuse DictionaryService.require_active_item(AttachmentCategory) and SystemSettingsService.get_attachment_max_upload_size_bytes; do not hard-code active categories or upload size.

storageSemanticsToFreeze.sourceSSOT: Current TypeScript contracts/service/repository/providers and original Nest behavior; shared types and OpenAPI remain TS-owned
storageSemanticsToFreeze.location: storageProvider + storageBucket + storageKey only. Session/attachment has no providerConfigId or frozen endpoint/key credentials.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.selection: Default lookup enabled=true/isDefault=true; absent -> implicit local. Present but not active -> BadRequest. Existing locations select provider+bucket configs, then longest normalized matching keyPrefix, retaining repository createdAt DESC ties; lookup does not filter enabled/status. Local without bucket and no match -> implicit local; non-local without match -> NotFound.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.prefix: Convert backslash to slash, trim leading/trailing slash; append exactly once for new default plan. Existing location is already prefixed. Prefix matching uses segment boundary, not arbitrary startsWith.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.defaultAndLocationConstraints: Enabled provider location unique on provider_type/coalesce(bucket,'')/coalesce(key_prefix,''); exactly at most one enabled/default globally. Creation/default set can change the previous default's isDefault and updatedBy. Disabling/misconfiguring clears default; set-default requires active+enabled. Do not modify any preexisting global default during fixture setup/cleanup.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.local: Root defaults to storage/attachments resolved against process CWD, overridden by POMS_ATTACHMENT_LOCAL_ROOT. File writes overwrite exact path; path lexical containment is checked after slash conversion and resolve. readObject stats then opens a stream, head returns size/mtime with null eTag/contentType/checksum; delete unlinks one key. testConnection creates .poms-storage-test-UUID at root then removes it. No recursive cleanup is justified.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.secret: Reuse AES-256-GCM v1 envelope and exact options: ATTACHMENT_STORAGE_PROVIDER_SECRET_KEY -> POMS_SECRET_KEY -> JWT_SECRET -> dev fallback, first nonempty without trimming; attachment-specific unreadable message. API and audit expose only configured booleans/timestamps, never ciphertext or plaintext.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.configSecrets: Create only accepts nonempty trimmed secret strings if supplied; update distinguishes absent/nullable clear/new value. credentialsUpdatedAt changes when either key is supplied. toDetail configured flags are based on ciphertext presence, not attempted decryption. testConfig catches decrypt/provider errors into failed result, while direct runtime location use may surface an unreadable BadRequest.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.OBS: Node fetch + custom SigV4. Preserve forcePathStyle vs bucket-host URL, endpoint base path/query, key path encoding, canonical headers/query sorting, SHA256/HMAC strings and signed headers. Presigned PUT uses UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, optional content-type/x-amz-meta-sha256, TTL floor clamp 1..3600 seconds, but expiresAt response remains supplied session expiry.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.OBSResponse: 404 -> NotFound exact message; other non-ok -> BadGateway with whitespace-collapsed response body truncated to 300 JS characters; GET body streams, missing stream -> BadGateway. HEAD reads content-length/eTag/last-modified/content-type and x-amz-meta-sha256 fallback x-obs-meta-sha256.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.OBSRetry: Only fetch throws retry up to 3 attempts with delays 250ms then 500ms, same signed request/body. HTTP 4xx/5xx responses are not retried. Do not import AWS SDK default retries or GH Axios protocol/error/proxy behavior as a premise.
storageSemanticsToFreeze.remove: Product AttachmentStorageService.remove swallows errors as best effort and keeps DB authoritative. Test cleanup must separately prove object absence; a swallowed product error is no zero-residue receipt.

uploadAndVersionSemantics.create: Sanitize original filename/extension, require dynamic max size and category/target access, freeze operation+metadata+provider/bucket/key/mode; expiresAt=createdAt+3600000ms. create-version resolves latest active group and copies effective category/security/first-link target.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.get: Only checks session access; does not transition expired sessions or remove objects.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.target: Expected version check before nonterminal/expiry. Pending->uploading is saved before generating target, so later sign/decrypt failure can retain uploading. Proxy returns POMS PUT path; OBS produces presigned PUT. multipart is not newly implemented by this batch.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.proxy: Only pending/uploading, nonterminal/unexpired, proxy mode; exact body byte count, SHA256 equal to existing declared string or set computed checksum; storage write precedes uploaded state/save. Raw body is not JSON. No expectedVersion body is defined for proxy upload.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.complete: Owner/access/version/terminal/expiry checks; validating save occurs before try. HEAD size must match; declared checksum compares metadata checksum only when present, otherwise declared checksum is accepted. With no declared checksum, read full object and compute SHA256. Do not silently strengthen checksum verification in migration.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.completeCommits: Attachment+link or new-version+old-latest+copied-links flush, audit insert, and completed session flush are distinct from validating and catch->failed flush. Failures can leave a real attachment/audit/object with failed session. Root must preserve and compare these facts rather than rolling them back in fixture normalization.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.terminalAndExpiry: completed/failed/expired/aborted terminal; receive/complete detects expiresAt<=now, saves expired+failedReason then throws409. Expiry does not delete object. Abort completed throws409; only nonterminal abort best-effort removes, saves aborted and audits. Abort failed/expired/already-aborted does nothing and can leave objects.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.versions: Version group fallback attachment.id; allocate latest.versionNo+1, clear old latest, new row latest=true/final=false, previousAttachmentId=latest.id; copy active links. Keep DB unique version number and partial active latest/final constraints and optimistic row_version.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.finalAndVoid: mark-final clears other group finals; clear-final requires reason and clears group finals; void clears final, reassigns latest to first other active in repository version order; it does not delete stored object. Audit and returned read can fail after actual mutation.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.links: link requires readable existing attachment + target write, repeats exact active relation idempotently; unlink requires exact link belongs to attachment and target write, soft-unlinks once, then calls getAttachment. Last-link unlink can persist and audit before returned read fails. No physical delete API.
uploadAndVersionSemantics.dormantNonHTTP: Legacy uploadAttachment/uploadAttachmentVersion methods have no current controller callers and are not two extra operations. copyActiveLinksToTarget is called by LeadService conversion; that real cross-domain consumer remains R3 scope with original caller transaction semantics.

acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.oldEvidence: Keep tools/rust-r2gh and tmp/rust-r2gh original receipts immutable. Any reuse occurs via new IJ modules or explicit imports that do not mutate old evidence. No GH run can count as new IJ runtime acceptance.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.completeReferenceGuard: Carry C-G3-02 pre-first-DELETE check inside verified transaction after requests settle: frozen full table catalog, locks, complete incoming-FK shapes including source schema/ordered multi-columns/target/update-delete actions/match/validated/deferrable/deferred. Preserve UUID/text/JSON compact-uppercase logical reference closure for all base + IJ + owned target seed rows. Unknown references/FK/catalog/identity mismatch reject before DML.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.guardExtension: The existing function's ownership keys are GH-only. IJ must register exact table/id/identity for provider config, upload session, attachment, link, dynamic audit/security rows and any target seed rows, preserve base/subtree rules, and extend frozen incoming-FK targets from original migrations. Do not simply call GH guard and claim IJ coverage, drop unknown relations, filter cardinality=1 or use actor/prefix adoption.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.globalDefault: Before creating default fixture configs, prove controlled DB and absence of unowned default; refuse or use new dedicated DB if any unowned default exists. Product API can demote previous default globally. Never repair test setup by clearing all defaults or deleting preexisting provider rows.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.objectLedger: Durable intent before each owned local/OBS PUT or controllable connection-test temporary object; store backend/run/environment identity, exact provider/location/config identity, expected bytes/SHA256, originating session/attachment and state transitions. Preserve result/error and observed current hash. Prefix alone never grants ownership.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.objectDeletion: Preflight every candidate and DB logical reference before first file/object delete or DB DELETE; require exact registered location, expected hash/size, owned row identity and no foreign references. Changed/unknown object, unresolved stream writes or ambiguous ownership blocks. Exact local containment and no symlink escape, exact key deletion only; no recursive directory/bucket/prefix cleanup. OBS requires controlled synthetic endpoint, never live deployment credentials.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.residuals: Failed/expired/aborted/completed upload residue is meaningful product state, not blanket cleanup permission. Record all expected/actual orphan objects with hashes, then clean only owned originals after assertions. Product best-effort remove does not prove absence. Perform repeat DB+local/controlled-OBS zero checks and preserve interrupted/failed rounds with real labels.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.cipherFaults: Port OwnedCipherFaults discipline to attachment_storage_provider_config encrypted_access_key_id and encrypted_secret_access_key: exact new owned row+column+identity+original/fault hashes, durable record before update, actually prove decrypt fails, normalizer only recognizes registered bad hash, finally restore only cipher columns, verify original ciphertext and plaintext fingerprint, retain real version/audit/last-error effects. Unknown cipher value or unrestored fault blocks cleanup.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.timestampPolicy: Create IJ explicit allowlist for only server-owned DB/DTO/audit fields, not arbitrary requestSnapshot/description/business/provider strings. Preserve ordinary ISO text literally; fact sorting only explicit table array paths. Assert upload session createdAt/expiresAt difference=3600000ms and actual send/receive bounds; signed URL X-Amz-Date/X-Amz-Expires/supplied expiry relation uses original floor/clamp semantics, not a blanket timestamp marker.
acceptanceSafetyCarryForward.expectedSafetyCounterexamples: Unknown scalar/JSON compact uppercase reference to owned upload/attachment/target, unknown/composite/foreign-schema FK, exact-ID identity alteration, same-count different table, unregistered default, changed object bytes or path, interrupted journal write, restore mismatch; each must reject with zero attempted destructive action. These are future IJ tests, not run or claimed here.
